{{recipe}} 

Salmon fillets are marinated in jerk spices, such as Scotch bonnet peppers, allspice, cinnamon, nutmeg, thyme, and ginger.

== Ingredients ==
* 4 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. (24 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]]) [[Cookbook:Salmon|salmon]] fillets with skin on one side
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]] [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]]
* 2 Scotch bonnet or habanero [[Cookbook:Chiles|peppers]], stemmed and seeded if you like
* 1 ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 1 ½ tsp freshly-ground [[Cookbook:Black Pepper|black pepper]]
* ¼ tsp freshly-ground [[Cookbook:Grains of Paradise|Grains of Paradise]], or more pepper
* ½ tsp freshly-ground [[Cookbook:Allspice|allspice]]
* ½ tsp freshly-ground [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]
* ¼ tsp freshly-grated [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|nutmeg]]
* 8 sprigs [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* A heat-resistant towel tied with twine and soaked in oil

== Procedure ==
#In a [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]] or [[Cookbook:Food Processor|food processor]], purée all ingredients except salmon, and oil until smooth. With the machine running, slowly drizzle in the oil.
#Pour into a gallon size zip-top bag. Add salmon and refrigerate for at least 10 minutes.
#Heat about 28 charcoal briquets in a large chimney starter. Disperse evenly around the bottom of the [[Cookbook:Grill|grill]].
#Reapply the grate. Quickly grease the grate with the towel.
#Add the salmon skin side down and cook, covered, turning often, until pink throughout and flakes easily when tested with a fork.
#Remove to a plate and cover with [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|aluminum foil]]. Let rest 5–7 minutes before serving warm.
